title: Federated Identity: what it uses
lede: One arrow for each component this feature lists. The steps reuse the feature's own "how it works" text; nothing here is a new claim. Internal and confidential: this text comes from an internal Ping deck and has not been tested on our tenant.

steps.title: Platform-issued tokens
steps.what: Supported platforms are Kubernetes service-account tokens, GitHub Actions and GitLab CI job tokens, SPIFFE JWT-SVIDs, and any platform that issues OIDC tokens with published keys (Federated Identity is the updated term; the release slide retires Non-Human Identity).
steps.why: Agents hold stored API keys that outlive their workloads and stay valid from anywhere if they leak.

steps.title: One credential for MCP, A2A and LLM
steps.what: The token stops at the gateway and is never forwarded; backends receive the application's own configured credential (static, per-user from the vault, or OAuth), and revoking the identity cuts the workload off immediately, with every request attributed to a specific deployment in audit.
steps.why: Agents hold stored API keys that outlive their workloads and stay valid from anywhere if they leak.

steps.title: Five deployment models
steps.what: Five deployment models are described: direct token read from a Kubernetes projected volume, per-job CI/CD tokens, SPIFFE/SPIRE for mixed estates, a stored agent key as the fallback where no verifiable token exists, and sidecar injection for agents you cannot modify, which is in development.
steps.why: Agents hold stored API keys that outlive their workloads and stay valid from anywhere if they leak.

steps.title: Issuer key-set handling
steps.what: Issuer and subject are matched exactly, such as one ServiceAccount in one namespace or one repository on one branch, and the audience is mandatory, so a key bound to main cannot be used by a pull request from a fork; additional claims such as repository, workflow and environment can be pinned.
steps.why: Agents hold stored API keys that outlive their workloads and stay valid from anywhere if they leak.

steps.title: Key owned by an identity, which supplies the…
steps.what: An agent access key can name a Federated Identity as the principal it acts as instead of borrowing a human owner, so a fully autonomous agent gets a real principal in audit and policy, and that identity supplies the verification material for the key.
steps.why: Agents hold stored API keys that outlive their workloads and stay valid from anywhere if they leak.
